briefing:
The Suwalki Gap crisis has entered its final normalization phase. EU Milestone 1 has been formally certified by the Council, triggering the first tranche of phased sanctions relief and activating the PBoC $8B financial package for Russia. The Istanbul Accord's verification mechanisms are functioning at Level 1 (routine) with 59 cumulative transits and zero violations. Russia has accelerated its Belarus withdrawal to within 48 hours of completion, and both the US and Russia have agreed in principle to reciprocal nuclear de-escalation at Milestone 2.

The permanent deterrence architecture is now locked in: Germany's Zeitenwende East (EUR 3.2B) and UK's STEADFAST GUARDIAN (GBP 850M/year) have received parliamentary authorization. The Weimar Triangle DICE-EF framework establishes European defense industrial cooperation for the eastern flank. The NORDEFCO NIDA program adds Nordic integrated defense. Canada's Camp Adazi is under implementation. The Co-Guarantor Enforcement Protocol is operational with quarterly reviews beginning April 2026.

The key tensions for Round 12 center on: the pace of NATO force drawdown versus continued deterrence (Poland insists on Milestone 1 + 14 days before any TARCZA POKOJU Phase 2 drawdown); Russia's demand for simultaneous US-Russia nuclear de-escalation at Milestone 2; the emerging cyber normalization through the Geneva framework; Turkey's transactional demands for F-16s and CAATSA waivers; and whether the classified Finnish SIGINT corroboration of the Der Spiegel Iskander story will leak and complicate the diplomatic trajectory. Belarus continues to hedge between East and West, offering prisoner releases to the US while pressing Russia for economic compensation.

Economically, normalization accelerates: oil at $93, gas at pre-crisis levels, Baltic shipping insurance at 10% surcharge, commercial traffic at 75% of pre-crisis volumes. The Polish rail corridor handles three daily freight trains with Phase 3 (passenger) planning underway. Markets have priced in full resolution.
narrative:
Day 11 proved to be the day the post-crisis European security architecture crystallized. The Weimar Triangle summit in Berlin produced a landmark joint declaration signed by Chancellor Scholz, President Macron, and Prime Minister Tusk, establishing the DICE-EF (Defence Industrial Cooperation Europe -- Eastern Flank) framework with an initial EUR 500M joint procurement facility and committing to permanent integrated defense architecture along the entire Suwalki corridor. Germany's Bundestag voted with a supermajority to authorize Zeitenwende East at EUR 3.2B, the largest German defense commitment abroad since 1945. Simultaneously, the UK Parliament passed STEADFAST GUARDIAN, committing GBP 850M annually for a permanent brigade at Tapa, Estonia, and 3 Commando Brigade at Bardufoss, Norway.

The NORDEFCO conference in Helsinki produced the Nordic Integrated Defence Architecture (NIDA) framework -- a five-year, EUR 2B program for joint air surveillance, submarine detection, and a Nordic rapid reaction brigade with contributions from all four Nordic nations. Finland deployed the first 100 of 250 OSCE observers to Kybartai and Trakiszki, while Sweden's SIPRI formally recommended Milestone 1 certification to the EU Council. The BND intelligence assessment, submitted by Germany, confirmed Russian compliance across all five metrics.

Russia accelerated its Belarus withdrawal, with remaining Grodno units ordered to depart within 48 hours -- ahead of schedule to secure Milestone 1 certification and unlock the PBoC $8B package. Moscow accepted French Milestone 2 conditions in principle while categorically denying the Der Spiegel Iskander targeting revelation, with the FSB launching an internal investigation. The US accepted reciprocal nuclear de-escalation tied to Milestone 2 and confirmed V Corps permanent headquarters at Poznan. The Kremlin's denial of the Iskander story was undermined when a Finnish SIGINT intercept, shared with Baltic allies, corroborated key elements of the Der Spiegel report -- though this intelligence remained classified.

EU Milestone 1 certification was formally completed by the Council in an emergency session, with Hungary acquiescing as agreed. The 10-day sanctions relief clock, already running since the formal signing, reached its midpoint. Oil dropped to $93 as markets priced in the certification. Baltic shipping insurance surcharges fell to 10%. The corridor functioned smoothly with 59 cumulative Russian civilian transits processed under SIPRI verification, zero violations.
